Description: craft_ui::theme::aphrody::visuals(dark, high_contrast) returns complete egui Visuals (surfaces, text, selection, state layers, shadows, M3 corners) from the canonical palette
Do: Install the visuals once and again when the mode or contrast preference changes
Don't: Build egui Visuals with hand-picked colours

Description: craft_ui::theme::aphrody::Tokens::get(dark, high_contrast) names every chrome colour (panel_fill surface, window_fill surface-container, dock surface-container-high, focus secondary, accent_border primary, scrim, window_shadow)
Do: Take panel window dock focus and selection colours from Tokens
Don't: Derive chrome colours by lightening the panel colour
Code Good: let tokens = Tokens::get(dark, high_contrast); painter.rect_filled(rect, shape::WINDOW, tokens.dock);

Guideline: Use Palette roles for custom painting
Description: Palette::get(dark, high_contrast) caches the scheme of Theme::aphrody_request (the product seed); palette.color(Role) returns an egui Color32 and palette.warning() the harmonized extended role
Don't: Keep a second palette or regenerate the scheme every frame

Guideline: Keep document and media colours app-owned
Description: The shared palette covers application chrome only; canvases, documents, media previews, diagnostics and saved appearance settings stay with each editor
Do: Theme toolbars panels and dialogs; leave the canvas colours to the engine
Don't: Recolour user documents or media with chrome roles
Code Good: let chrome = Tokens::get(dark, hc).panel_fill; let canvas = document.background;
Code Bad: let canvas = Tokens::get(dark hc).panel_fill; // overrides the document

Description: craft_ui::theme::shape exposes CONTROL (small), MENU (extra-small) and WINDOW (medium) corners from aphrody-m3-tokens; apply_control_to_visuals sets the control corner on every widget state
Do: Use shape::CONTROL MENU WINDOW and apply_control_to_visuals when installing custom visuals

Guideline: Use M3 state layers for interaction
Description: The visuals compute hovered and pressed fills as state layers of the content colour over the control and give the active widget the M3 focus indicator thickness in the secondary role
Do: Rely on the installed visuals or WidgetPalette for hover press and open states
Don't: Change only the border or text colour on hover
Code Good: WidgetPalette { noninteractive, inactive, hovered, active, open }.apply_to(&mut visuals.widgets, shape::CONTROL, stroke);

Description: buttons::IconButton::new(label, size, &IconButtonStyle) paints the icon through a closure and returns egui::Response; selection wins over press and hover, and egui keeps pointer capture
Do: Build toolbar buttons with IconButton and an accessible label
Don't: Use an unlabeled ImageButton for tools
Code Good: IconButton::new("Brush", Vec2::splat(32.0), &style).selected(active).show(ui, |ui, rect, tint| paint_brush(ui, rect, tint))

Description: icons::SvgIconSet prepares compiled-in monochrome SVGs once (currentColor and stroke-width substitution) and serves them by URI; use a distinct URI prefix per catalog and style
Do: Keep one SvgIconSet in a OnceLock and install egui_extras image loaders with svg
Don't: Rebuild icon bytes per frame or reuse one URI prefix for two styles

Guideline: Use craft-ui layout and docking helpers
Description: layout provides toolbar fitting, split geometry and resize handles; tabs handles tab fitting; docking supplies transactional panel moves
Do: Use the shared toolbar split and docking helpers for editor chrome
Don't: Write a new splitter or dock per editor
Code Bad: // custom drag-resize code in each app

Description: Palette and Tokens have high-contrast variants (the request at high contrast) and the visuals switch borders to the outline role
Do: Pass the OS high-contrast flag to visuals and Tokens

Description: egui, eframe and egui_extras come from the workspace dependency table (0.36.2) with default features off; the Craft editors share craft-ui
Do: Declare egui = { workspace = true } in the crate
Don't: Pin a different egui version in one editor
